extracted.intended_audience: Lutheran theologians, clergy, and delegates representing the Evangelical (Lutheran) side before a Church council; confessing Christians seeking doctrinal standards
extracted.subtask_description: A concise confession (The Smalcald Articles) drafted by Martin Luther setting out non-negotiable doctrinal positions and practical reforms to be presented by Lutherans at a Church council; intended to indicate what may be accepted or must be rejected. Focuses on doctrines of Christ, justification, sacraments, papacy, and various abuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublime Articles concerning the Divine Majesty (Trinity and Incarnation)
rubrics_metrics.description: I. That Father, Son, and Holy Ghost, three distinct persons in one divine essence and nature, are one God. II. That the Father is begotten of no one; the Son of the Father; the Holy Ghost proceeds from Father and Son. III. That not the Father nor the Holy Ghost but the Son became man. IV. That the Son became man by conception of the Holy Ghost and was born of the pure, holy Virgin Mary; afterwards suffered, died, descended to hell, rose, ascended, sits at the right hand of God, will come to judge, etc., as the Apostles' and Athanasian creeds and common Catechism teach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These articles are acknowledged on both sides and need no further contention; they represent the orthodox baseline of Christian faith which the authors accept without dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification by faith alone (chief, non-negotiable article)
rubrics_metrics.description: That Jesus Christ, our God and Lord, died for our sins and was raised again for our justification; that all are justified without merit by His grace through the redemption in Christ's blood; faith alone justifies (Rom. 3, 23 ff.; Rom. 4, 25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This article is the first and chief article and cannot be yielded or surrendered under any circumstances; it undergirds all opposition to the Papacy and related practices. 'Of this article nothing can be yielded or surrendered.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of the Mass as a sacrificial work
rubrics_metrics.description: The Mass in the Papacy is the greatest and most horrible abomination because it conflicts with the chief article: it has been held that the Mass, even if rendered by a wicked person, frees men from sins in this life and in purgatory—claims contrary to Christ as the sole Lamb of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Mass, insofar as it is regarded as a human work that merits forgiveness or reconciles to God, must be condemned and rejected; this point cannot be conceded in discussions with papal authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass is a human invention and unnecessary; may be omitted without sin
rubrics_metrics.description: The Mass is but a pure invention of men and has not been commanded by God; it is unnecessary and can be omitted without sin or danger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preach publicly that the Mass as men's twaddle can be omitted without sin, and that one can be saved in a better way (according to Christ's institution). Doing so will cause the practice to collapse among reasonable, God-fearing people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquish the Mass to prevent abuses (commercialization of masses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Innumerable and unspeakable abuses have arisen from the buying and selling of masses; therefore the Mass should be relinquished to prevent abuses even if it had something advantageous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of the systemic corruption (masses sold for money), giving up the Mass is warranted to stop these evils; this practical consideration supports condemnation of the Mass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private self-administration of Communion and private use without Word/Church communion is improper
rubrics_metrics.description: If one administers the Sacrament to himself as an act of devotion, it is a human notion, uncertain, unnecessary, prohibited; to use the common Sacrament apart from the Word and apart from the communion of the Church is trifling with it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communion must be administered according to Christ's institution and in the context of the Word and Church; private improvisation or self-communing is condemned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purgatory and masses for the dead are unsupported and to be rejected
rubrics_metrics.description: Purgatory and the practices connected with it (masses for souls, vigils, annual obsequies, Common Week and All Souls Day, soul-baths, sacrifices for the dead) are a specter of the devil and conflict with the chief article since they treat the Mass as the means of aiding the dead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no divine command concerning the dead; such practices may be safely omitted even if they were not errors. One must not frame articles of faith from the Fathers without Scripture; the Word of God alone establishes articles of faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority of Scripture alone to establish articles of faith
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule is: The Word of God shall establish articles of faith, and no one else, not even an angel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements of the Fathers (e.g., Augustine) cannot be pressed into articles of faith without Scripture; confessional/doctrinal standards must be grounded in Scripture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appearance of spirits claiming to be departed demanding masses is deceptive and cannot justify practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Evil spirits have perpetrated knavery by appearing as departed souls demanding masses, pilgrimages, alms, etc., things which were taken as articles of faith and confirmed by the Pope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such supernatural-sounding claims do not establish doctrine and are to be rejected; they illustrate the dangers of accepting practices apart from Scripture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilgrimages are unnecessary and harmful
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilgrimages were practiced to obtain masses, remissions and grace; they are not commanded by the Word, are unnecessary, uncertain, pernicious, distract from parish duties and the Word of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preach that pilgrimages are not necessary but dangerous; encourage people to remain in their parish and offices ordained by God rather than run after such practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraternities that assign and sell masses and works are human inventions and intolerable
rubrics_metrics.description: Fraternities (societies) where cloisters, chapters, vicars assign and communicate masses and good works for living and dead by legal contract are human baubles, without the Word of God, unnecessary and contrary to the chief article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such contracted assignment of salvific benefit is to be rejected and not tolerated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relics are spurious and should be condemned
rubrics_metrics.description: Relics contain many falsehoods (bones of dogs, horses, etc.) and have been revered as if they worked indulgence and forgiveness; they are without the Word of God and should have been condemned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if some good exists in relic veneration, because they are unsupported by Scripture and lead to superstition and idolatry, they must be repudiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indulgences sold for money are corrupt and must be rejected
rubrics_metrics.description: Precious indulgences granted (but sold for money) to living and dead sell the merit of Christ and the merits of the saints; they are without the Word of God, unnecessary, and contrary to justification by grace through faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indulgences as commercialized remission must be condemned; justification is by grace through faith, not by money or papal power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invocation of saints is idolatrous and destroys knowledge of Christ
rubrics_metrics.description: Invocation (calling upon) of saints, making festivals, masses, offerings, altars, and regarding saints/angels as helpers and patrons is not commanded by Scripture and constitutes idolatry; it destroys the knowledge of Christ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although saints may pray for others, Christians are not to invoke or adore them; honor may be expressed in Christ but not divine worship or trust in saints for salvation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapters and cloisters should be restored to original useful purposes or abandoned
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapters and cloisters, originally founded to educate learned men and chaste women, ought to be turned back to such uses to produce pastors, preachers, ministers, and well-educated maidens; if they will not serve that purpose, they should be abandoned or razed rather than continued with blasphemous services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monastic institutions must be repurposed to serve the church and commonwealth; they must not be upheld as superior to ordinary Christian life or callings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pope is not supreme head of all Christendom by divine law
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pope is not, according to divine law or the Word of God, the head of all Christendom (that name belongs to Christ alone); he is only bishop and pastor of the Church at Rome and of those voluntarily attached to him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The claim of papal supremacy by divine right is a human figment, unnecessary and not commanded; bishops historically addressed the Pope as brother. The Church can exist without such a head.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Papacy is diabolical/Antichrist in its claims and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: All things the Pope has done from his false and arrogant power are diabolical and aimed at the ruin of the Christian Church and the destruction of the chief article of redemption; the Pope's teaching exalts him above Christ and approaches the office of Antichrist (2 Thess. 2, 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the Papacy usurps Christ's place, claims to bind salvation to obedience to the Pope must be resisted; the authors will not submit to such claims even unto death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original sin: total hereditary corruption from Adam
rubrics_metrics.description: Sin originated from Adam by whose disobedience all men were made sinners, subject to death and the devil (original or capital sin). The hereditary sin corrupts nature so deeply that reason cannot understand it and must be believed from Scripture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject scholastic assertions that natural powers remain entire, that man by nature has right reason and good will, or that man can by nature observe all God's commands; such views make Christ's death needless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of the Law: to restrain sin, reveal original sin, and drive to repentance (not to justify)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Law was given by God to restrain sin by threats and punishments and to reveal original sin and its fruits; its chief office is to make man see his corruption and need for grace; the Law 'worketh wrath' and increases sin insofar as it reveals the depth of corruption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Law exposes sin and drives to despair/humble repentance; it does not justify (that is the Gospel's office).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of true repentance (passiva contritio) and the Gospel's promise
rubrics_metrics.description: True repentance is not manufactured (activa contritio) but passiva contritio — a deep, humbling sorrow of heart, a breaking by God's hammer (the Word) that leads to despair of self and anxiety for help; immediately the New Testament adds the consolatory promise of grace through the Gospel: 'Repent and believe the Gospel.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repentance must be understood as profound contrition wrought by the Law, accompanied by faith in the Gospel promise of grace; this is the path to salvation, not reliance on works or rites.
